forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.previous_feedback: Previous vetter reason: The proof correctly establishes the floor identities for all k with 1 <= k < n and for k = n, using valid bounds that force each quantity into the interval [k-1, k) or [n-1, n). The argument is complete and matches the lemma statement exactly.
payload.previous_proof_nl:
Let n > 1 be an integer and let r be a real number with (n - 1)/n <= r < 1.

First, let k be any integer with 1 <= k < n. From r < 1 we get kr < k. Also, since r >= (n - 1)/n, we have
kr >= k(n - 1)/n = k - k/n.
Because k < n and n > 0, we have k/n < 1, so k - k/n > k - 1. Therefore
k - 1 < kr < k.
Since k - 1 is an integer, this implies floor(kr) = k - 1.

Now take k = n. From r >= (n - 1)/n we get
nr >= n - 1,
and from r < 1 we get nr < n. Hence
n - 1 <= nr < n,
so floor(nr) = n - 1.

This proves that for every integer k with 1 <= k < n, floor(k r) = k - 1, and also floor(n r) = n - 1.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let n > 1 be an integer and let r be a real number with (n - 1)/n <= r < 1.

We first handle integers k with 1 <= k < n. From r < 1, multiplying by the positive integer k gives kr < k. Also, from r >= (n - 1)/n we get
kr >= k(n - 1)/n = k - k/n.
Since k < n, we have k/n < 1, hence k - k/n > k - 1. Therefore
k - 1 < kr < k.
Because k - 1 and k are consecutive integers, any real number strictly between them has floor equal to k - 1. Thus floor(kr) = k - 1 for every integer k with 1 <= k < n.

Now take k = n. From r >= (n - 1)/n we obtain nr >= n - 1, and from r < 1 we obtain nr < n. Hence
n - 1 <= nr < n.
Therefore floor(nr) = n - 1.

This proves the stated floor identities.
result_payload.proof_summary: For 1 <= k < n, the assumptions imply k - 1 < k r < k, so floor(k r) = k - 1. For k = n, the assumptions imply n - 1 <= n r < n, so floor(n r) = n - 1.
